title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 27-29): Grothendieck is trying to say exactly what extra structure the motivic Galois group carries for motives over a field k contained in C. He wants to know which abstract data come from an actual category of motives.

The data a)-g) of p. 27:
- a) An algebraic group G over Q (Aut_tensor of the Betti fibre functor). It comes with a weight cocharacter i: G_m -> G and a 'Tate/Lefschetz' character eps: G -> G_m.
- b) G'' = Aut_tensor(T_Hdg), the automorphism group of the bigraded Hodge fibre functor over k.
- c) Two cocharacters i1, i2: G_{m,k} -> G'' with eps(i1(l)) = eps(i2(l)) = l and i1(l)i2(l) = i(l). These are the (p,q)-bigrading, i.e. the two components of the Hodge cocharacter of the Deligne torus.
- d) A torsor Q under the unipotent group H''. H'' is the group respecting the filtration attached to the bigrading and acting trivially on the graded pieces.
- e) The de Rham-Betti torsor P under G' = Aut_tensor(T_DR).
- f) An identification G tensor k = ad_{G'}(P), compatible with i and eps.
- g) A complex point phi in P(C): the period comparison isomorphism.

This page runs the dictionary backwards, under the Hodge-conjecture hypothesis (cf. 3)).
- Think of the motives M as Rep(G), with T_B the forgetful functor. Define T_DR := P x^G (T_B tensor_Q k), a twisted form, so that G' = Aut_tensor(T_DR).
- There is then a unipotent subgroup H' of G' and a bitorsor Q under (H', H''). One has T_Hdg = T_DR x^{H'} Q and G'' = Aut_tensor(T_Hdg). The cocharacters i1, i2 bigrade T_Hdg.
- Since H'' is defined by i1 (filtration by p, identity on gr), the bigrading descends to a filtration on T_DR: the Hodge filtration, defined over k. Note Q is trivial because H' is unipotent, which matches the NB of p. 27.
- Extending scalars gives a filtration on T_DR tensor_k C. The period isomorphism phi carries it to T_B tensor_Q C, so every Betti realization V_C gets a filtration.

Conditions on a)-g):
- 1) For every representation V of G (equivalently a faithful one), this filtration on V_C makes V a Q-Hodge structure. That is, the filtration is opposite to its complex conjugate, with weight given by i; 'conditions annexes' presumably means polarizability. In modern terms, the phi-transported Hodge cocharacter defines a homomorphism S -> G_R, i.e. a point of a period domain.
- 2) The resulting Hodge structure is (probably) 'motivique', i.e. of geometric origin.
- 3) A descent condition. The k-structure on V_C given by T_DR via phi must correspond to a descent (restriction of scalars) from C to k of the motive over C determined, via 1) and the Hodge conjecture, by the Hodge structure.

NB: Grothendieck notes that 2) and 3) cannot be expressed directly in terms of the data. The page breaks off with 'On trouve alors, si on admet la conjecture de Hodge, que tous ...'.

The next page continues: the image of the identity component of pi_1 must lie in the Q-subgroup generated by i1, i2, i.e. the Mumford-Tate group. It also adds a 2*pi*i rationality condition on the period of the Tate motive.

Purpose: an early Tannakian / period-torsor axiomatization of 'Hodge realization data' of motives over k. This is the precursor of Deligne's systems of realizations and of the description of Hodge structures by cocharacters of the Deligne torus.
errors: A filtration on V_C transported by phi does not by itself give a Hodge structure. One needs opposedness to the conjugate filtration (complex conjugation from the Q-structure), the weight compatibility via i, and polarization. Grothendieck leaves these as 'conditions annexes', so condition 1) is only sketched.

'For every representation (or one faithful one)': the equivalence is correct but unargued. It holds because the filtration is split by a cocharacter of G_C, so subrepresentations of tensor constructions are strict.

Condition 2) ('motivique'/'multiplicatif') and 3) are not formulated in terms of the data, as Grothendieck himself admits. So the characterization is incomplete: it is a heuristic dictionary, not a theorem.

ideas.what: Motives over k described by a group G/Q with a de Rham torsor P, an inner form G' = ad(P), and a complex period point phi in P(C)
ideas.modern_name: period torsor / Tannakian comparison torsor Isom(T_B tensor k, T_DR); systems of realizations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (period conjecture, 1966 footnote); Deligne (1979 periods, 1989 Tannakian, realizations); Saavedra 1972; Andre
ideas.where_published: Only indirectly (footnote on periods in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties', 1966; Recoltes et Semailles mentions motivic Galois group)

ideas.what: Hodge bigrading encoded by two cocharacters i1, i2 with i1*i2 = weight cocharacter and eps*i1 = eps*i2 = id; the Hodge filtration comes from i1 via a unipotent group H'' and is transported to Betti via phi
ideas.modern_name: Hodge structure as homomorphism of the Deligne torus S -> G_R (Hodge cocharacter mu and its conjugate); parabolic/unipotent radical description of filtrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Theorie de Hodge II 1971, Travaux de Shimura 1971); Mumford 1966; Saavedra 1972 (filtered fibre functors)

ideas.what: Conditions for abstract data to come from motives: every representation is a Hodge structure, it is 'motivic', and the k-de Rham structure is a descent of the complex motive (assuming the Hodge conjecture)
ideas.modern_name: characterizing motivic Hodge structures with k-structure; absolute Hodge / Hodge-de Rham realization criteria

ideas.what: Torsor under a unipotent group over a field is trivial, so Q is trivial and G' and G'' are isomorphic (splitting of the Hodge filtration over k)
ideas.modern_name: triviality of unipotent torsors over affine bases

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly poses the problem of characterizing intrinsically, in terms of the Tannakian/period data a)-g), which data come from motives over k. He notes that the 'motivic' condition and the descent condition cannot be expressed in terms of the data. This is an early form of the still-open problem of recognizing motivic Hodge structures and their fields of definition.
missed.quote: NB On ne sait pas expliciter 2) et 3) directement en termes des données a), ... !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, this places in 1965 a Tannakian formulation of 'realization data + period point' with explicit open recognition criteria. That predates Deligne's systems of realizations and Saavedra's filtered fibre functors.

missed.claim: A 1965 formulation of Hodge structures via a pair of cocharacters (i1, i2) of the automorphism group of the graded Hodge fibre functor, with i1*i2 = weight, together with a period point in a de Rham-Betti torsor. This is essentially the Deligne-torus / Hodge-cocharacter formalism usually dated to Mumford 1966 and Deligne 1971.
missed.quote: i_1, i_2 : G_{m,k} -> G'' définissant une bigraduation sur T_Hdg ... cette bigraduation correspond à une filtration sur T_DR
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Priority / attribution detail: Grothendieck's unpublished notes already contain the group-theoretic encoding of Hodge structures and period torsors that underlies Mumford-Tate groups and Shimura data.

deep.surprise_reason: Not a new theorem, but a notable unpublished early (1965) Tannakian axiomatization. It combines a period torsor, a complex period point, Hodge cocharacters i1/i2 and conditions for being motivic, predating Mumford 1966, Deligne 1971 and Saavedra 1972. It plausibly circulated orally to Deligne, which tempers the surprise.
transcription_corrections: Condition 2): the underlined word read as 'multiplicatif[?]' is more plausibly 'motivique' ('Ce dernier est motivique'). This fits the NB that 2) cannot be expressed in terms of the data.
'On φ définit une [?] de ce dernier' is likely 'Or φ définit une iso[morphisme/bijection] de ce dernier sur T_B ⊗_Q C'.
The line 'On s'imagine M comme Rep(G), T_B (comme le foncteur oubli sur Rep(G))' appears not to be struck out; only the title line 'Hypothèses conjecture de Hodge' is crossed.
In 'T_DR comme P ×^G (T_B ⊗_Q k)', the struck symbols are an initial 'T_B' and a '×' replaced by the contracted product with G written above.
